subject.title: Telegram should default to allowlist mode with owner ID

question: Should fresh Telegram setup move to token-verified owner capture that writes dmPolicy="allowlist" and allowFrom by default, or should omitted Telegram dmPolicy continue to mean pairing with stronger manual allowlist guidance?
rationale: This chooses the first-run trust boundary for a bundled private Telegram bot and affects compatibility for users who rely on pairing as the omitted-policy behavior.

options.title: Adopt token-verified fresh setup default
options.body: Generate a short setup token, accept only the matching Telegram message as owner proof, write allowlist config for fresh or implicit setups, and preserve explicit pairing configs.

options.title: Keep pairing default
options.body: Current pairing remains the omitted-policy default while setup and docs more strongly route one-owner deployments to manual numeric allowlists.

options.title: Fold into broader bootstrap design
options.body: Keep this issue as narrow context while the broader bootstrap or post-bootstrap auto-flip issues define the permanent product contract.

recommendation.title: Adopt token-verified fresh setup default
recommendation.body: Generate a short setup token, accept only the matching Telegram message as owner proof, write allowlist config for fresh or implicit setups, and preserve explicit pairing configs.
